In light of changing priorities and shifting to a more simple lifestyle, last summer I decided to finally pare down my decades old library that I had lugged with me several times across the country over the years. I knew it would be a lengthy process and rather than give myself a set number of books to keep or a certain number of bookshelves to fill, I decided my first step would be to reread everything I own, rate it on a scale of 1-5 and let myself keep only the ones rated 4 and 5. (Generally 4 stars = amazing writing OR an amazing story, 5 stars = amazing writing AND an amazing story; basically these are the books I know I want to reread again in phase 2 of "the Great Paring" which won't be for another couple of years lol)

As the pile of "3 and under" rated books grew (and I inwardly cringe at some of the books that added weight to moving boxes being hauled up and down stairs, time and time again) I decided before I donated them I would start cataloging the books I read since they would no longer be living on my shelf. After I entered the first few books with just a plain old "fiction" tag, I decided I would also start tagging more specifically, including with the decade I first read the book (teens, twenties, thirties, etc). Once I finished I realized two things:

  1. I've read 50 books in the last 8 months (that number came as a delightful shock) and
  2. The themes of the books I read, when sorted by decade when I first read them, was a strikingly accurate capture of that period of my life.

I'm not sure if I was influenced by what I read or if I chose books reflecting my life but it's a tagging system I will definitely continue to use and I look forward to looking back on it over the years. I don't really have a specific question, just something I thought other lifelong bibliophiles may empathize with :)
